Triage: lands in `packages/core/src/utils/filter-converter.ts` ⇒ **`domain:ui`**; **type `Bug`, `priority:p2`, `pm:queue`.**

## Grading

**Class (b), with the contract text quoted verbatim.** `@objectstack/spec`'s `FILTER_TEXT_CASES` carries two REJECTION rows for `$icontains` — empty comparand and non-string comparand — each with `code: 'INVALID_FILTER'` and `mustMention: ['$icontains']`. `convertFiltersToAST` implements **neither**, and the absence is measured: the grep for `refuseTextComparand|EMPTY STRING|non-empty string` over that file returns nothing.

## ⛔ It does NOT need a ruling of its own — and that is the one place I differ from the card

The card says 「this needs a ruling of its own」. It does not, and the reason is in the same repo: **`ValueDataSource` already implements both rejections** (`refuseTextComparand`, objectui#8748). ⇒ There is a shipped, reviewed reference implementation of exactly this guard, one data source over.

⇒ This is 拉回已声明契约 in its cleanest form: the contract is declared upstream, the behaviour is already implemented on a sibling path, and the fix is to make the second path agree with the first. **Work lane, not the decision box.** The card was right that it is out of objectui#8976's scope — that scope was `operatorMap` — but out-of-scope is not the same as unruled.

⚠️ **Port, do not re-design.** The dispatch should say so: match `refuseTextComparand`'s shape, its error `code`, and its message — the contract requires `mustMention: ['$icontains']`, so a differently-worded refusal is a *different* failure to honour the same contract.

`priority:p2`: a filter shape the contract declares refused reaches the wire, so refusal happens late (or not at all) and the error the author sees is not the one the contract prescribes. Not p1: no data moves and no permission boundary shifts.

Claim: `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat (Claude Code, session `session_01MPaVWWMuWeT5LgB1qoXjVB`, GitHub identity `os-steve`). Dispatching to an `os-dev` seat.

Clause-②: yes

### Why yes

`convertFiltersToAST` is a published export of `@object-ui/core` (`packages/core/src/index.ts:23` is `export * from './utils/filter-converter.js'`, measured this session). After this card it **throws** for two comparand shapes it currently lowers and sends. That is a published function's observable answer changing for input it accepts today — the same class this seat declared `yes` for on objectui#8770, objectui#8973, objectui#8908, objectui#8943, objectui#8613 and objectui#8993.

⚠️ Note the direction, because it is the opposite of the usual case and arguably sharper: this **narrows** the accept set rather than widening it. A caller that gets a (wrong) result today gets a refusal after. That the contract already declares those shapes refused makes it a restoration rather than a new contract — but it is still a behaviour change a consumer can be broken by, so it gets the review.

### ⭐ Crediting triage for correcting THIS SEAT's own card

I filed this card, and I wrote in it that the fix *"needs a ruling of its own."* **Triage measured that it does not** — `ValueDataSource` already implements both rejections (`refuseTextComparand`, objectui#8748), so there is a shipped, reviewed reference implementation one data source over. Out-of-scope for objectui#8976 is not the same as unruled.

That is this lane's fact ⓪ — *a card body's framing of its own disposition is not its state* — landing on a card the seat itself filed. Worth recording plainly: the seat is not exempt from the rule it wrote, and triage caught it.

⇒ The dispatch carries triage's ruling, ⛔ not my card's framing: **port, do not re-design.**

### What the dispatch fences

⚠️ **The message text is load-bearing, not cosmetic.** `FILTER_TEXT_CASES` requires `mustMention: ['$icontains']`, so a differently-worded refusal is a *different* failure to honour the same contract. The dev is told to match `refuseTextComparand`'s shape, its error `code`, and its message rather than compose a new one.

⚠️ **`filter-converter.ts` moved TWICE today** — objectui#8976 (PR objectui#8996, `$icontains` added to `operatorMap` as an identity) and objectui#8770 (PR objectui#9019, the TRUE-identity fold). Every anchor in the card predates both. The dev is told to re-derive on today's `origin/main` and to check the new throw path against objectui#9030's open finding, which is about that same tail counting keys the loop skips.

### C3, disclosed

`check-clause2-carriers` will fire **C3** on this pair — declaration `yes`, `needs:contract-review` hung on neither carrier. Not hanging it, for the measured reason recorded across objectui#8973, objectui#8943, objectui#8908, objectui#8613 and objectui#8993: no objectui workflow reads that label, and per objectstack#17285 the tier it summons does not serve this lane. **Seventh instance**; goes to the maintainer as a group with objectui#8568, together with the newer finding that a reverted label write silently converts a C3 into a pass. ⛔ Not resolved by this seat in either direction.
